title: kdash calendar
description: Payload of kdash:calendar — latest-value TS-OWNED (STRING JSON, no TTL), exactly 2 segments, on central (KDASH_CENTRAL_REDIS). The TAGGED days for kpidash's time and calendar card: Ken's personal days off, holidays and special days, already expanded to concrete dates. The panel draws the clock, the month grid and the weekends itself; this feed carries only the dates that have something to say. Contract v1 (CD-30). Yearly repeats and holiday rules are the publisher's business: every entry is one concrete date, and the reader does no date arithmetic beyond comparing `YYYY-MM-DD` strings. All dates are local calendar dates in America/Los_Angeles, the home's timezone, NOT the fleet hosts' UTC system clock; a consumer computes `today` in that zone before comparing. Freshness: tags change rarely, so an old `ts` is a muted hint at most and NEVER a reason to blank the calendar; the real stale condition is a window [`from`, `to`] that no longer covers today (kdash_calendar_covers). Field names are pinned; a rename, retype or removal lands as kdash:calendar:v2 (rules.md Versioning), never in place.

ts.description: Unix seconds (float) when the publisher built the record, writer's clock. Bounded at 1e11 so a millisecond stamp fails instead of reading as permanently fresh.

expected_refresh_s.description: How long the publisher expects between its own scheduled writes, in seconds; 3600 for an hourly publisher (it also writes on every change to the list). A reader MAY mute the card's tag colours once `ts` is older than this plus its grace (kdash_cadence_stale); it must keep drawing the last good record either way.

from.description: First date the record covers, inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD`: the first day of the current month at `ts`, so the whole visible month is always inside the window.

to.description: Last date the record covers, inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD`: at least 90 days after `ts`'s date. Never before `from` (a producer obligation; the C reader rejects a record that breaks it). A date in [from, to] with no entry in `days` is AFFIRMATIVELY untagged; a date outside it is unknown.

days.description: One entry per TAGGED date inside [from, to], sorted by date ascending, each date at most once; ONE entry carries all of that date's tags (a day off that is also a birthday is one entry with `off` true and `special` set). An untagged date is simply absent, and weekends are never listed for being weekends. Every entry carries at least one tag — `off` true, `holiday` or `special` — and lies inside the window; both are producer obligations the validator cannot check (no anyOf, no date comparison: CD-24), and the C reader skips and counts an entry that breaks either. Empty when nothing in the window is tagged.

off.description: A personal day off for Ken. Independent of `holiday`: a holiday Ken works is `off` false, and a holiday he takes is `off` true with the holiday named.

holiday.description: The holiday's name (`Thanksgiving`). Absent when the date is not a holiday; never null, never empty. A holiday falling on a weekend is listed on the date itself, and the weekday it is OBSERVED on is its own entry whose name says so (`Independence Day (observed)`). Two holidays on one date are joined into this one string by the publisher.

special.description: A special day's name (`Ken's birthday`, an anniversary). Absent when there is none; never null, never empty. Two on one date are joined into this one string by the publisher.

short.description: Optional label for tight spaces (`Thanksgiving`, `Bday`), at most 12 characters, chosen by the publisher for the entry as a whole. Absent means the card has no short label and picks its own fallback; it never truncates `holiday` or `special` into this.

x-counterexamples.why: `off` is required on every entry; a holiday Ken works still says `off: false`
an untagged holiday is ABSENT, not null — null is not a holiday name
`short` is at most 12 characters; a label that will not fit the tight space is not a short label
a locale date; every date on this feed is `YYYY-MM-DD`
`off` is a boolean, not a word
`to` absent: a record that does not say where its window ends cannot say a date is untagged
a millisecond `ts` would read as permanently fresh
`expected_refresh_s` absent: the writer must declare its cadence (CD-28)
